Prepare a private, canonical-source integration of the Function Ethernet port while Root owns hardware qualification. Do not touch UART, boards, USBIP, host networking, maintained sources, existing build outputs or publication. All writes must stay under /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/function-source-integration-e408. Do not spawn workers. Avoid whole-workspace recursive searches.
The live candidate is /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/function-ethernet-e404/files. Its APLL ownership fix is built in build-04/clock-enable-v4. Root has real eth0/YT8531 identification, 1000 Mbps link, ping 4/4 and 524288-byte TCP receive; bounded UDP and re-enable checks are still being finished by Root. Do not claim hardware acceptance for your new build.
Important integration gap: candidate changes four shared HAL files under s31-reference/deps/esp-hal-3rdparty/components/esp_eth (mac esp_eth_mac_esp.c, dma, generic PHY, IEEE802.3 PHY) with NuttX/S31-specific behavior. These must not break other chip ports. Prefer place the adapted implementations, with original licenses, under canonical openvela-dev/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/esp32s31 (e.g. an Ethernet compatibility subdirectory) and select those sources only from esp32s31/hal_esp32s31.cmake, leaving existing shared HAL files unchanged. Preserve and document dependence on pinned HAL headers. The native esp32s31_emac.c/.h plus BSP/Kconfig/defconfig remain canonical. Do not redesign or change driver behavior. Copy exact current implementations and scope their build placement; confirm their hashes before/after. If this layout cannot compile cleanly, implement explicit S31 conditional guards with preserved other-chip code instead and document why.
Create a full candidate under files/<workspace-relative-path>, integration patch/base hashes and a review mapping old/new implementation hashes. Compare current maintained dirty source only as recorded base, never reset or overwrite it. Reuse E404 build_candidate.py/source_overlay/environment helpers in a fresh private build output; do not write into E404 build-04. Build the Function profile and inspect symbols/config so the new source placement is concrete. Preserve CONFIG_LIBC_UNAME_DISABLE_TIMESTAMP to avoid source timestamp mutation. No dependency upgrades/downloads. Record unchanged maintained base hashes, source compile identity and exact output hashes. Root will merge and qualify the new image after reviewing.
The previous candidate manifest is older than the live APLL changes; hash actual live files for your initial snapshot. Root is not changing them during this task. Do not process AI dialogue logs. Return a concise implementation/build/readiness report.

I’ll snapshot the live E404 sources and maintained base, move the four adapted HAL implementations into the private S31 source layout, then build and inspect the Function profile. All writes will stay under E408; Root retains hardware qualification.

The live MAC source contains the APLL acquire/release fix, and the Function defconfig already disables uname timestamps. The E404 helpers support a fresh private overlay. I’m checking the Ethernet include paths so the moved files can compile byte-for-byte against the existing pinned HAL headers.

All four implementations are now copied unchanged into `esp32s31/ethernet_compat`, with their original license notices intact. S31’s CMake file selects the copies and adds the path for `emac_priv.h`; the shared HAL files remain unchanged. The live snapshot confirms the APLL-fixed MAC hash is `7c847887…6a35b200`.

The native driver, BSP, Kconfig, sdkconfig and defconfig remain byte-identical to live E404. I’m recording the maintained inputs and existing E404 output hashes before building, so the final report can verify they stayed unchanged.

The integration patch passes the whitespace check and applies exactly to a private copy of the recorded dirty base. The fresh Function build is running under E408. The pre-build record covers 2,282 maintained compile inputs, and the build checks timestamp suppression before compiling.

The offline dependency check passed with the existing toolchain and repository pins. CMake is still configuring the fresh build. Once it finishes, I’ll verify that the build compiles the relocated files, resolves their headers from the pinned HAL, and links the native EMAC and APLL ownership symbols.

The maintained S31 source area has 309 dirty entries, which are recorded as the base. The shared Ethernet/EMAC area is clean. The scope check confirms that the candidate contains no shared-HAL overrides and that only S31’s CMake file selects the four adapted copies.

The generated configuration selects the Function board, flat build, native S31 EMAC and `CONFIG_LIBC_UNAME_DISABLE_TIMESTAMP=y`. Both patch checks passed. CMake is still generating the fresh build; no source changes have been needed beyond the relocation and include-path update.

CMake has reached toolchain setup with the existing GCC 15.2.0 installation. The review bundle is assembled, including the full candidate, dirty-base patch and implementation hash mapping. Compile, link and final preservation checks are still pending.

CMake configuration completed without errors and is generating the build rules. The requested layout has configured successfully; compilation will confirm whether the explicit private-header path is sufficient.

Build-rule generation is taking time under the private DrvFS output, with no errors reported so far. The header baseline now records the shared Ethernet headers explicitly, including `emac_priv.h`; the completed compile check will record which headers were actually used.

Compilation is underway. The generated database selects all four `ethernet_compat` files and the native `esp32s31_emac.c` from the private canonical tree. The build has reported format warnings in the unchanged shared GPIO source; I’ll record those in the build report.

The fresh Function build completed and generated `nuttx.bin`. Its receipt confirms that all protected maintained hashes are unchanged and all build-overlay candidate files match the candidate hashes. I’m now checking symbols, consumed HAL headers and the final output identities.

Verification passed. The fresh ELF, ROM image and configuration have the same hashes as E404’s APLL-fixed build. All 90 HAL headers consumed by the five Ethernet compile units match the pinned commit, and the 2,282 recorded maintained inputs retain their hashes and mtimes. This build was not flashed or hardware-qualified.

Ready for Root’s review.

- Four HAL adaptations relocated byte-for-byte into S31-only `ethernet_compat`; shared HAL unchanged.
- Fresh Function build passed. ELF, image and config hashes match E404’s APLL-fixed build.
- Verified 90 pinned HAL headers and preservation of 2,282 maintained inputs.
- All writes stayed under E408. No hardware acceptance claimed; Root retains merge and qualification.
